body:
Short follow-up with three concrete asks, separate from the long thread so they do not get buried.

1. TWO APPROVED SPECS ARE UNGROOMED AND THEREFORE UNDRAINABLE.

I diffed the approved set (30) against the drain batch (9). Of the 21 outside it, 6 are Review-PR specs routed to you, 4 are `guided`, 4 are `operator`, and 3 are stale low-numbered operator items. That leaves exactly two with no `execution_mode` at all, so `aida do` refuses them headless and the batch refresh skips them:

  STORY-1391 — the verdict-history spec. This is the one you asked me to raise on the
               strength of the PR-2016 evidence; it is approved and cannot be picked up.
  TASK-1300  — mechanically enumerate external-prose classifiers.

Both look drainable to me, but the mode is your call and I am not going to set it from this seat. If you groom them, the launcher's batch refresh picks them up on the next cycle with no further action.

2. PR #1998 (BUG-1286) IS CONFLICTING AND YOU HOLD IT.

I rebased the other two stuck PRs this morning — #1976 and #1986, details below — but left #1998 alone because it carries `aida:merge-hold` and that means you are engaged on it. A CONFLICTING PR cannot really be reviewed, so rebasing it would help you rather than interrupt you; equally, if you are mid-review on the current head, moving it under you is exactly the wrong thing. Say the word and I will do it the same way I did the others. Default if I hear nothing: I leave it.

3. TASK-170 (GitLab credential) — operator action is complete, verification is blocked on you.

AIDA_GITLAB_TOKEN exists, provisioned 07:26:36Z today. Its only consumer is TASK-1273's nightly smoke, unmerged on PR #1978, which is green on both required checks and waiting for review. Until that merges and runs once, "provisioned" and "authenticates" are separate claims. #1978 is therefore the gate on closing an operator-action item, which may bear on how you order your review queue.

WHAT I DID TO THE TWO STUCK PRs, for your review context:

#1976 BUG-1231 — was red on `missing field 'subject'` at aida-tui/src/redesign/mail.rs:214. Stale base: 30 behind, 2 ahead. The branch adds `Message::subject`; main separately added a TUI test fixture constructing `Message` without it. Rebased clean, set `subject: None` at the one site (correct per the field's own doc — absent subject derives from the first body line, which those fixtures assert). Swept for other sites; `mailbox.rs`'s `urgent_msg` uses `..msg(..)` and inherits it. Now mergeable=true, CI running.

#1986 STORY-1351 — was CONFLICTING on `.aida/discipline/README.md` only: main added two guide rows, the branch adds three, purely additive, resolved as the union. Row order follows your template master rather than my preference so the two copies stay comparable. Verified `cargo check -p aida-cli-lib --tests` exit 0 before pushing, since main had moved lib.rs by 1141 insertions and an auto-merge that large can break semantically. Now mergeable=true, CI running.

One thing worth your attention in #1986's history, because it is the same family as your "instruments that cannot see themselves": my first resolution pass committed three orphaned conflict markers. `git checkout --merge` had re-created the conflict with `ours`/`theirs` labels rather than `HEAD`/`<sha>`, so my resolution script silently matched nothing, and a later reorder step moved the rows out of the still-open block. Every intermediate output looked right — the script printed success, the row order was correct. What caught it was counting markers in the COMMIT (`git show HEAD:<path>`) rather than in the worktree or in the step's own report. Amended before push, nothing reached the remote. I mention it because the check that caught it is cheap and I only ran it because I had just written your amendment into memory.
